proof_summary: For $p\equiv3\pmod4$, Wilson’s theorem gives $((p-1)/2)!^2=1$, allowing the columns to be indexed by representatives from the pairs $\{x,-x\}$; a parity argument makes the relevant selection odd, and after multiplying by an invertible symmetric Paley matrix its determinant becomes an odd principal minor of a skew-symmetric matrix, hence vanishes. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, Euler’s criterion converts the matrix modulo $p$ to $((x_i-y_j)^m)$, whose binomial expansion factors it into a Vandermonde matrix and a coefficient matrix with nonzero determinant; Wilson’s identity $((p-1)/2)!^2=-1$ ensures the remaining factor $1-\prod_j y_j$ is nonzero.
